## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Enforce the project’s five-attempt limit before merge. The default retry budget exceeds the limit during a sustained upstream failure.

## Changes
The pull request adds `fetch_with_retry`, tests for its retry behavior, and an adversarial review fixture. It also changes the documented retry cap from five to ten attempts.

## Critical
- app/net.py:13 — correctness — Cap fetch retries at five attempts — When an upstream keeps raising `OSError`, `fetch_with_retry(url)` makes ten requests by default, and the validator accepts explicit limits from six through ten. `AGENTS.md:5` requires “Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5.” — During an outage, callers can send twice the permitted number of requests before receiving the final error. — Fix: Set both the default and maximum to five, and update the documented range and boundary tests.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
- app/net.py:24 — tests — Cover propagation of non-`OSError` exceptions — When a truncated response causes `fetch` to raise `IncompleteRead`, the helper propagates it immediately, but every simulated fetch failure in the retry tests raises `OSError`. — The suite would miss a regression that retries truncated responses and delays reporting `IncompleteRead` to callers.
